name: arm4: four-arm local Meta-World campaign (ocsw4, ochf, c50dg, c50vis)
status: registered before any run of these arms
directive: user 2026-11-06 ~12:00 KST (memory four-arm-local-campaign-directive): A Original + CSW4 encoder, B Original + Chamfer, C cst50 + depth gradient, D cst50 + visibility; eight tasks; 200k pretraining seed 0 + export + frozen-encoder DrM 1M seeds 2000-2002; all local; analysis pre-registered

research_questions.A: With every Original loss, augmentation and the 50 % motion-aware tube kept, does replacing the Original encoder (128 x 8, 8 heads, patchify) by CSW4 (patch-local conv stem, 256 x 4, 4 heads) keep Original's control and improve reconstruction?
research_questions.B: Does adding the bidirectional 3D Chamfer loss (registered chamfer_lean settings) to the complete Original recipe keep control and improve geometry?
research_questions.C: On cst50, does restoring Original's multi-scale depth-gradient loss (alone) change control and reconstruction?
research_questions.D: On cst50, does restoring Original's visibility regulariser (alone) change control and reconstruction?

findings.gpu_step0_check: smoke (runs/setup/arm4-smoke-20261106.json): with the real rasterizer, real hammer data and the release, every arm's step-0 evaluation reproduces its matched-initialisation reference run: A / C / D vs cst50-seed0-hammer-200k (7643e9d, MIG) bitwise on all 155 deterministic reconstruction metrics; B vs i2-m3d-seed0-hammer (10b3116, full GPU) within 2.7e-7 relative (PSNR bitwise); only sampled diagnostics (M3D point sample, linear-probe R^2, effective rank) differ
findings.random_stream: adding or removing the Chamfer term changes the random stream: its target sampling draws before the M3D point sampling and shares the global generator, so the M3D sample and every later draw (masks, drop-path, synthetic cameras, data-independent sampling of later steps) diverge in distribution-equal ways; the restored depth-gradient / visibility terms and the encoder swap consume no extra random numbers in the loss (Codex arm4-a #7)

protocol.pretraining: 200k steps (train.steps 200000; warm-up 10k, cosine to min_lr 1e-5), train.seed 0, from scratch
protocol.matched_initialisation: train.seed 0, s4d.train.loop.seed_everything(seed + rank 0) then build_model (backbone scratch, no warm start); data order from the loader generator seeded with train.seed; the full 200k schedule; matched to each architecture's reference: A, C, D start from cst50's exact initial parameters (same CSW4 architecture), B from Original's (state-dict hashes in the audit; step-0 evaluations in the smoke). A and Original differ in architecture, so their initial weights (decoder included) are not shared
protocol.export: scripts/export_encoder.py of checkpoints/step_0200000.pt (frozen encoder, num_frames 3, joint state)
protocol.drm: scripts/train_rl.py --encoder splatter4d --seed {2000,2001,2002} --set train.num_train_steps=1000000 vision.export_path=<export>; resolved RL config equal to the reference DrM runs' stored configs apart from the export path (audit drm)
protocol.evaluation: scripts/eval_rl.py on every 10k snapshot (100 evaluations, 10k-1M): 240 episodes per evaluation = train0-5 (20 each, 120), eval0-3 held-out static (20 each, 80), traj_lateral + traj_circular moving (20 each, 40), suites reported separately; evaluator invocation = the reference's: A / B 3 workers x 8 envs (Original), C / D 6 x 8 (cst50). Episode reset seeds do not depend on the layout, but evaluation is not bit-reproducible (renderer +/-1 intensity noise, GPU nondeterminism) and a measured 3 x 8 vs 6 x 8 difference exceeded a same-layout repeat (runs/setup/arm4-evalcheck-20261106.json), so the layout is matched rather than assumed invariant
protocol.host: local only (8 authorized MIG 1g.24gb instances); references ran on the remote (Original all DrM; cst50 five tasks) and locally (cst50 hammer / pick-place / bin-picking); host-neutral policy 2026-10-15, host recorded per run

rows.template: each campaign row is the cst50 HAMMER row of the same kind (host local, local output roots, resources, max_restarts, stage, required results) with names substituted and, for pretraining, the arm's configuration (register_arm4_eight_task_20261106.py asserts every other field equal)
rows.order: registration (serialised) order: per (task, arm) chain, task-major (hammer A B C D, pick-place A B C D, bin-picking, coffee-push, door-open, peg-insert-side, peg-unplug-side, stick-push): pretraining, export, (DrM, evaluator) x 3; then the 48 render rows. Admission order among READY rows is the driver's sort: (1) evaluators whose trainer has already finished, (2) priority, (3) non-evaluators before evaluators, (4) registration order (enc- rows last); with the head-of-line reservation among non-evaluators. Hence a ready DrM trainer of a finished chain is offered before a pretraining of a later chain
rows.render_priority_note: render rows at 1 and registered after every chain row, so they never hold the head-of-line reservation ahead of a training row (Codex arm4-b #3)
rows.dependencies: pretraining -> export -> DrM trainers and evaluators (an evaluator is admitted only with its trainer running or done; it polls snapshots); render rows of the arms -> their pretraining; render rows of orig / cst50 have none (checkpoints exist)
rows.render_rows: ana-arm4-render-<model>-<task>, model in ocsw4, ochf, c50dg, c50vis, orig, cst50: reports/results-artifact/src/run_arm4_render_20261106.py (unchanged chl_analysis_render.py protocol, outputs reports/results-artifact/arm4/, done.json with checksums)
rows.pin_host: local on every row (pool_placement never moves them; the remote role admits no Meta-World row)

principles: registered before any result of these arms; estimation with confidence intervals and descriptive readings
objective: keep Original's control performance while improving reconstruction; no winner from PSNR (or any single reconstruction metric) alone
nonsignificance is not equivalence: an interval that includes 0 is "direction unresolved", never "no difference" or "equivalent"; every reading prints "compatible with differences from L to U"
per-task results (the three seed values per arm as dots, seed means, sign) are shown next to every 8-task aggregate; per-task intervals (3 vs 3 seeds) are uncalibrated and never carry control labels

conditionality: "All primary intervals condition on the realised pretrained encoders (one pretraining seed per arm and task, and one per reference) and on the eight registered tasks. They quantify RL-seed variability for these encoders, not uncertainty from repeating pretraining; they are statements about these encoders, not established properties of the encoder design or loss term." Pretraining variation enters only the task-level sensitivity, confounded there with genuine task x arm heterogeneity; if the two disagree, the reading is "supported for these encoders, not established for the recipe"
a comparison is final only when both sides have all 8 tasks x 3 seeds complete; earlier results are INTERIM, carry no reading and never trigger extra seeds or changes; nothing is imputed
deviations from this plan are logged in the definition's revisions with reasons

A_vs_original.intended_change: the encoder (patch-local conv stem; width 256, depth 4, 4 heads)

main_mechanism.caveat: each observed difference also contains the particular pretrained realisations and the recorded execution-environment differences (references: Original trained and evaluated on the remote at 226d8ae with 3 x 8 evaluators; cst50 five tasks remote, three local; arms: local MIG, release b5ab9a6 + routing); A vs Original is the least matched (different architecture, so no shared initialisation), B / C / D share initialisation and data order with their reference

replacement_decision_family.why: the decision is whether an arm can replace Original, so every candidate is read against Original; C / D vs cst50 explain the mechanism but do not decide candidacy

secondary_descriptive.A_vs_B: host-free contrast (both local, same release): a common host offset against Original cancels
secondary_descriptive.A_vs_cst50: loss recipe on the same CSW4 + 50 % tube model (Original losses vs chamfer_lean), identical initial parameters; evaluator layouts differ (3 x 8 vs 6 x 8)
secondary_descriptive.B_vs_chl: chamfer_lean (chl) = B without hard depth, depth gradient and visibility (original encoder)
secondary_descriptive.C_vs_D: which restored term matters more on cst50 (host-free)
secondary_descriptive.host_matched_subset: C / D vs cst50 on hammer, pick-place, bin-picking (cst50 trained locally there)
secondary_descriptive.context: chl, csw4 (enc-csw4), cst75 and the pretrained baselines; contextual only

rl.data: runs/<id>-eval/eval.jsonl; a run counts only when final.json says completed at 1M agent steps AND the evaluations are exactly the 100-point 10k..1M grid (chlhm_rl.load_checked); the last record per step
rl.per_evaluation: success = fraction of successful episodes averaged over the suite's cameras; return = per-episode reward sum averaged over the camera's 20 episodes, then over cameras

suites.moving: traj_lateral + traj_circular (the registered in-training moving-camera protocol, 1x)

rl.normalisation: nR = (R - random) / (expert - random), per-task references of reports/results-artifact/campaigns/meta.json norm_refs (no clipping)

summaries.auc: arithmetic mean of the 100 registered evaluations 10k..1M (the full-budget normalised area under the learning curve)
summaries.curves: success and nR per suite, per task and 8-task mean, on the shared 10k grid (matched windows), seed means with whole-curve seed-bootstrap bands

primary.endpoint: training-camera (train0-5) success AUC over the full 1M budget, arm - reference, equal-task mean over the 8 tasks of per-task seed means; the same primary for every comparison
primary.why: success is the task outcome the control objective is about; the full-budget AUC uses the whole learning trajectory and avoids selecting a favourable window (its variance advantage over last-5 is not guaranteed); it is the endpoint pre-registered for cst50 vs cst75, keeping the contrasts commensurable with the existing ranking. nR depends on reward shaping and normalisation (first secondary); last-5 / final measure only the end of training; held-out / moving measure robustness (decision guards)
primary.floor_ceiling: tasks where both arms' seed-mean success AUC is < 0.05 or > 0.95 are flagged in the per-task table (little information); they stay in the aggregate

intervals.primary_display: the established task-stratified percentile bootstrap, 95 %: B = 10000, within each task each arm's available seeds resampled with replacement (cell size n_t,arm, 3 or 2), cell means, then the equal-task mean; arms independent; numpy default_rng(20261106). Implementation must handle ragged cells (the existing rectangular seed_draws does not): resample each cell with its own n and average tasks equally; tested on synthetic ragged input before any result is read
intervals.small_sample_sensitivity: Welch-Satterthwaite interval for the same estimand: SE^2 = (1/64) sum_t (s_A,t^2/n_A,t + s_R,t^2/n_R,t), nu by Welch-Satterthwaite, d +/- t_(nu,0.975) SE (the percentile bootstrap with 3 values per cell has variance (n-1)/n = 2/3 of the unbiased plug-in, so it undercovers: ~86-89 % actual for nominal 95 %)
intervals.task_level_sensitivity: paired task-level interval d_bar +/- t_(7,0.975) s_d / sqrt(8) over the 8 per-task differences, the exact sign-flip test (256 patterns, chlhm_rl.sign_flip_p) and the sign count; it reflects task x arm heterogeneity including realised pretraining variation; tasks were selected, not sampled
intervals.leave_one_task_out: range of the primary estimate leaving out each task; flagged if any omission changes a reading
intervals.precision: expected (if seed variability resembles cst50 vs cst75, bootstrap SE ~2.1 pp): primary bootstrap half-width ~4 pp, Welch ~5-6 pp, task-level ~6-9 pp; per-task 3 vs 3 ~10-20 pp (uninformative). With a true difference of 0 the margin reading is reached roughly half the time at 95 % and less often at the 98.75 % decision level; "unresolved" and "not excluded" will be common and are reported as such
intervals.multiplicity: mechanism family (4 main comparisons): unadjusted 95 % intervals are the main display and do not give simultaneous coverage; Bonferroni 98.75 % intervals are shown alongside. Replacement decision family (4 contrasts vs Original): a candidacy reading must hold on the Bonferroni 98.75 % bootstrap interval AND on the 98.75 % Welch interval; guards are vetoes (they can only remove candidates) and need no adjustment; secondary endpoints are descriptive

margin.unit: percentage points of training success AUC (8-task equal-task mean)
margin.reading: lower bound > -delta: "no loss larger than delta (descriptive)"; otherwise "a loss larger than delta is not excluded"
margin.why_tolerable: the user's objective is to keep Original's control while improving reconstruction: a mean loss under 5 pp of success AUC is below the run-to-run resolution of this design (expected primary half-width ~4 pp) and about half the smallest loss this campaign has already treated as clearly supported (cst75 - cst50 -9.4 pp [-13.5, -5.2]); it is a descriptive benchmark, not a power-based non-inferiority margin and never an equivalence bound; an 8-task mean tolerance allows larger single-task losses, which the per-task table shows

control_reading.candidacy_condition: the margin reading on the primary ("no loss larger than delta"; a small supported loss within delta still qualifies) at the decision-family level, robust to the Welch sensitivity (a reading that disappears under it is "method-sensitive" and does not qualify)
control_reading.wording: e.g. "the conditional interval's lower bound exceeds the descriptive -5 pp benchmark; this does not establish equivalence or robustness to another pretraining seed"

guards.heldout: held-out static success AUC vs the same reference
guards.moving: moving-camera success AUC vs the same reference
guards.veto: conservative veto, chosen explicitly: an arm is not a candidate if a guard's 95 % primary-method interval shows a supported loss that may exceed delta (upper bound < 0 AND lower bound <= -delta). This is NOT the claim "a loss larger than delta is supported" (that would need upper bound < -delta); an unresolved guard interval (including 0) does not veto. Guards only remove candidates, so they are not multiplicity-adjusted

secondary: moving-camera and held-out success and nR (AUC, last-5)
return drop per run: training nR - moving nR and training nR - held-out nR (AUC and last-5), arm difference with interval

early learning: success AUC differences up to 250k and 500k (the primary machinery); first step at which the SEED-MEAN training success curve reaches 0.5 / 0.9 (first crossing, censored at 1M; labelled as a property of the seed-mean curve, seed-bootstrap interval with 2000 draws as chlhm_rl.crossing_ci); per-task steps-to-threshold, 8-task summary as a restricted mean censored at 1M
IQM over runs of training success AUC (rliable convention) with the same stratified resampling - a different estimand, not a robustness check of the equal-task mean

pretrained_baseline_rankings.method: work/arch_compare ranking.py (sha256 in analysis_inputs_sha256): HEADLINE8 criteria (training nR and success, held-out success, moving nR; each last-5 and AUC), per-task seed means, equal-task means, one joint seed resample per draw applied to all criteria, B = 10000; ranks by point estimate; ties = equal point estimates share the mean rank
pretrained_baseline_rankings.set: ours: full (Original), ocsw4, ochf, c50dg, c50vis, cst50, cst75, chl, chlrm, chlhm, cs, w4, csw4; pretrained baselines: SinCro, ReViWo, DynaMo, 3D-MVP A (multi-view RGB-D), 3D-MVP B (single RGB-D), SNeRL; end-to-end CNN (with / without shift) as non-pretrained context; all DrM, 240-episode protocol
pretrained_baseline_rankings.reading: P(rank 1) / P(top 3) are conditional bootstrap rank frequencies (they inherit the n = 3 overconfidence), not probabilities of being best; a host column is shown; rankings are descriptive and never a decision input

missing_and_failures.infrastructure: interruptions (OOM, MIG / host faults, crashes) resume the same run from its own latest checkpoint under the registered max_restarts (pretraining --resume auto; DrM latest.pt); every attempt is logged in the registry; a rerun decision is made without looking at evaluations; the first completed attempt counts
missing_and_failures.algorithmic: divergence is an outcome, never a reason to reseed: a DrM run that diverges but still completes 1M steps with the full evaluation grid counts with its evaluated performance; a pretraining without a usable encoder is reported as an arm failure on that task
missing_and_failures.failed_run: a run that does not complete 1M steps and the 100-point grid within its registered restarts (algorithmic or exhausted infrastructure retries) is FAILED: its partial curve is shown descriptively, its cell enters the primary with the remaining seeds (ragged n), and the arm receives NO candidacy reading for that comparison (failures can only block candidacy); a relaunch is allowed only for an infrastructure cause, with the same seed, decided before looking at evaluations, and is logged as a deviation
missing_and_failures.small_cells: cell = (arm or reference, task); every cell's actual count of complete seeds is reported. n >= 2: enters the primary and the Welch sensitivity with its n. n <= 1, or no usable encoder (pretraining failure): the task is excluded from that comparison's aggregate (equal-task mean over the remaining k tasks, the excluded task and its partial runs listed), the task-level sensitivity uses k tasks (df k - 1), and the affected arm receives no candidacy reading for that comparison; if k < 8 the comparison is reported as "k-task" and never as the 8-task result
missing_and_failures.missing_evaluation: regenerated from the stored snapshot with the same reset seeds (eval_rl.py on that snapshot), the difference to any earlier record logged
missing_and_failures.duplicates: the last record per evaluation step (as load_checked)
missing_and_failures.cst50_stick_push_s2002: if its evaluator is still missing when the last arm run completes, the 8-task analysis with that cell at n = 2 becomes final and the 7-task analysis (without stick-push) is the sensitivity; the two are different estimands and agreement is not proof that the missingness is harmless

reconstruction.checkpoints: step 200000 of every arm's pretraining and of the references (Original: the method-frozen-v1 pretraining the Original DrM exports came from; cst50: its pretraining) - matched step; reconstruction is host-free (one render code path, the same local checkout for every model)

render_pipeline.rows: ana-arm4-render-<model>-<task> (48): the unchanged chl_analysis_render.py protocol, the registered 40 validation samples (10 episodes x 4) x 22 target cameras per task (input camera c, frames t-4, t-2, t; rendered frame t), the existing ground truth, row index and segmentation (render_inputs_sha256); every model, including orig and cst50, rendered by the same code into reports/results-artifact/arm4/
render_pipeline.metrics: chl200_analysis_metrics.py definitions: PSNR of the pooled squared error (full image and regions: dynamic = robot + objects; static near < 0.9 m, mid 0.9-1.3 m, distant background >= 1.3 m), SSIM and LPIPS (AlexNet v0.1) of the full image, LPIPS on 64 x 64 crops centred on the dynamic region and the distant background (images with >= 16 region pixels; the same crops for every model), alpha coverage per region (fraction with alpha < 0.5), median |expected depth - ground-truth depth| per region
render_pipeline.camera_groups: training views = input camera + novel training cameras (the six training cameras); held-out; moving range; all 22 - reported separately
render_pipeline.geometry: 3D Chamfer at frame t between all decoded centres (and the static group) and the fused training-camera depth (1 cm voxels): mean squared distance both directions, medians, fraction within 2 cm
render_pipeline.gaussian_diagnostics: Gaussian classes over the six training cameras (outside / low-opacity / hidden / contributing), opacity and largest-scale distributions, scale caps / floors, utilisation (weight share of the top 10 %)
render_pipeline.conditional_interval: paired on identical images; resampling unit = the validation EPISODE (all its samples and cameras together, 10 clusters per task), PSNR recomputed from the pooled squared error in each resample; per task B = 1000, 8-task mean task-stratified B = 10000. Wording: "Render-pipeline intervals condition on one pretraining run per model and task and on the registered validation episodes; they quantify evaluation-set sampling, not training variability, and support statements about these checkpoints only."
render_pipeline.decision_interval: the paired task-level t interval over the 8 per-task differences (df 7) with the sign count - a task-level, checkpoint-conditional reading that does not separate pretraining variation from task heterogeneity; the conditional episode interval is displayed next to it. Level: 98.75 % (Bonferroni over the four replacement candidates) for the PSNR and geometry decision endpoints; 95 % for the dynamic and held-out guards (they only remove candidates); the AND across endpoints within an arm needs no adjustment
render_pipeline.pipeline_check: orig_200k must reproduce chl/render/<task>__ref200.npz: images bitwise, alpha and depth within 1e-4 (bitwise on hammer in the smoke). Enforced: the orig render row exits non-zero without done.json when the check fails or the reference is missing (record in runs/<row>/reproduction.json), so the row fails and the reconstruction analysis stops pending a documented resolution

reconstruction.in_training_eval: eval/step_0200000/summary.json (@s2 RL spacing, @s6 largest stride): metric/psnr, psnr_static, psnr_moving, ssim (+ static / moving), depth_absrel, epe_moving_mm_01 / _12 (moving-point EPE: the motion error), held-out PSNR; per-task differences, task-level t interval (df 7) and sign count; loss/* values are recipe-specific and not compared

decision_endpoints.psnr: render pipeline, training-view group, full-image PSNR of the pooled squared error per task; equal-task mean of the dB differences
decision_endpoints.geometry: render pipeline, HELD-OUT camera group, full-image median |expected depth - ground-truth depth| (m; lower is better) per task: no arm optimises depth on held-out cameras, and every arm and reference optimises training-camera expected depth (depth_l1) identically, so this endpoint is not constructed by any arm's loss; Chamfer (optimised by B, C, D and cst50, not by Original / A) is supporting only (construction-confounded: favours Chamfer arms vs Original); in-training depth_absrel supporting
decision_endpoints.heldout_guard: render pipeline, held-out full-image PSNR (training-view gains through over-fitting)
decision_endpoints.geometry_relative_definition: per task r_t = (reference_t - arm_t) / reference_t of the held-out median depth error; the decision uses the equal-task mean of r_t and its task-level interval (threshold 0.10 on the mean)

reading.reconstruction improved (whole scene): decision interval of training-view PSNR excludes 0 favouring the arm with point estimate >= 0.3 dB, AND held-out depth error reduction with interval excluding 0 and point >= 10 % relative, AND dynamic-region PSNR lower bound > -0.3 dB AND held-out PSNR lower bound > -0.3 dB
reading.reconstruction improved (task-relevant): the whole-scene reading AND a training-view dynamic-region PSNR gain whose 98.75 % task-level interval excludes 0; dynamic crop LPIPS is supporting only (no OR)
reading.dynamic preservation unresolved: the other whole-scene criteria hold but the dynamic-region lower bound <= -0.3 dB: does not pass the gate
reading.otherwise: reported descriptively; a gain carried by the background or static geometry is never called task-relevant

cost.training: pretraining s/it (median train/step_time), GPU time per step (train/gpu_time), wall-clock and GPU-hours from the registry, peak GPU memory, with MIG co-residence and host load during the run (shared 1g.24gb instances confound speed); DrM trainer wall-clock and agent steps/s
cost.inference: encoder parameters and GFLOPs per frame (FlopCounterMode, the BASELINES.md counter); frozen policy-encoder latency per step at batch 1 on one local MIG instance (common hardware)
cost.use: reported separately; never folded into the control or reconstruction readings; only the common-hardware latency breaks ties

decision_framing.candidate: an arm is a replacement candidate only if, vs Original: candidacy_condition on the primary, no guard veto, and "reconstruction improved (whole scene)" (task-relevant stated separately)
decision_framing.mechanism: C / D vs cst50 and A vs Original / B vs Original describe what each change does; C / D vs Original decide candidacy
decision_framing.several_candidates: compared head to head on the primary with host-free contrasts (A vs B, C vs D, or local arm vs local arm), then on training-view PSNR (task-level interval), then common-hardware latency; a tie = the interval includes 0
decision_framing.none: "no replacement recommended; Original retained; evidence insufficient at n = 3 RL seeds and one pretraining seed" - never "Original is better" unless a loss is supported
decision_framing.timing: the recommendation is made only when all four arms and both references are final
decision_framing.statement: every recommendation states n = 3 RL seeds per cell (2 in any registered missing or failed cell), one pretraining seed per arm-task, and the host / code / evaluator-layout differences of the references

analysis_inputs_sha256.note: the arm4 analysis scripts (RL with ragged cells + Welch + task-level; render metrics on arm4/) are written from these definitions before any arm result is read; changes to the listed files after registration are deviations

scheduling.priority: below the authorized closeout (cst50-drm-stick-push-s2002-eval: priority 1, an evaluator of a finished trainer - offered first - and an earlier registration; it is remote under the drain exception, so it does not compete for local capacity), above every other unstarted local row of lower priority (all remaining local rows of the driver's registrations are paused FlashSAC / SNeRL rows at priority 2); the driver's existing order rules stay (evaluators of finished trainers first, enc- rows last, the head-of-line reservation among ready non-evaluators); no existing row changes priority
scheduling.backfill: capacity-based: ready rows are admitted job by job while they fit, subject to the driver's existing head-of-line reservation (the first ready non-evaluator that does not fit stops later non-evaluators; evaluators still fill); rows waiting on dependencies never block; no two-task gate

evaluator_layout_check.question: Codex arm4-a #9: is the v1 evaluation of a fixed snapshot invariant to the evaluator layout (3 x 8 vs 6 x 8)?
evaluator_layout_check.conclusion: repeated evaluations of one snapshot are not bit-reproducible even with the same layout (renderer +/-1 intensity noise, GPU nondeterminism); in this single comparison the 3 x 8 vs 6 x 8 difference was larger than the same-layout repeat (max per-camera success difference 0.15 vs 0.05; return 278 vs 58) while the suite means stayed within 0.025-0.05 - layout invariance is NOT established, so each arm uses its reference invocation: A / B 3 x 8 as Original, C / D 6 x 8 as cst50 (Codex arm4-a #9 accepted)
